The August 1, 2018 FOMC statement’s upbeat tone on growth and labor conditions is broadly corroborated by Beige Book signals: districts reported rising prices and inflation, with many expecting pricing pressures to intensify; labor markets are tight across occupations (engineers, manufacturing workers, IT professionals, truck drivers), prompting firms to raise compensation and focus on retention, with some districts noting longer work hours. Regional color remains favorable—Dallas buoyed by energy and strong consumer spending, Richmond reporting solid consumer spending, and St. Louis characterized by growth—while agricultural commodity prices show mixed moves.

Offsetting these positives, higher interest rates are weighing on existing home sales, and the April SLOOS points to selective tightening (wider loan rate spreads and CRE policy adjustments) amid largely steady standards for qualified jumbo mortgages. Netting strong activity and tightening labor/price pressures against housing sensitivity and modest bank-term tightening, the tone stays moderately positive with a cautious edge, consistent with gradual normalization. sentiment score = 0.70
